messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — saw repeated extra GPU nodes coming up in us-west-2 overnight even though autoscaler was off. total gpu nodes jumped from 18 -> 28 and cost alerts fired.
Priya Rao: Interesting, which provisioner is handling GPU requests? Karpenter or legacy nodepools? :thinking:
Marco V: KarpenterProvisioner 'gpu-prod' is active in that cluster. We migrated workloads last week.
Alex Chen: Right — cluster-autoscaler is disabled on those clusters. Karpenter should be the only scaler. Logs show a bunch of ScaleUp events with similar requirements (p4d,p4de), but many ended up as small p3s because constraints allowed multiple instance types.
Samir: Can you paste the karpenter controller events? I want to see if it was failing to bind pods and then over-provisioning.
Alex Chen: Paste of recent events: ```Warning FailedScheduling  pods "train-job-52" 0/20 nodes are available: 12 node(s) didn't match node selector, 8 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu. Normal Provisioning  Provisioning node for pod train-job-52 using provisioner gpu-prod```
Dina L: We were trying to be flexible with instance types to improve bin-packing across GPUs. Maybe that looseness caused multiple launches. Also region ENI limits may have blocked larger instance types, forcing Karpenter to attempt several smaller launches.
Priya Rao: If ENI/ENI IP exhaustion prevented p4d from becoming Ready, Karpenter could keep issuing more launches until a pod bound. We should look at instance startup failures in the ASG/instance events.
karpenter-bot: [event] provisioner/gpu-prod created instance i-0abc1234 (p3.16xlarge) - initializing
Marco V: Proposed quick mitigations: tighten the provisioner requirements to prefer specific instance families (only p4d,p4de) and set `consolidation: true` to let Karpenter reclaim fragmented nodes. Also set `limits.resources.cpu`/memory to guard against large overprovision.
Samir: Agree. Also add `ttlSecondsUntilExpired` on empty nodes so stray VMs don't sit forever. For spot/on-demand mix, use `capacityTypes: ["spot","on-demand"]` and `weight` affinities. But be careful with training jobs (SLOs) — mark them with `nodeSelector` for on-demand.
Alex Chen: Cost impact: overnight we saw ~12 extra GPU-hours at ~2.8x unit cost. If this recurs across clusters it's non-trivial.
Dina L: Longer term: run a small canary in eu-west-1 where ENI behavior is different. Instrument node lifecycle: add events to datadog for `Provisioning`, `FailedScheduling`, and `InstanceLaunchFailed` with instance-type.
Priya Rao: I'll open a Jira for the change and a follow-up RFC for conservative defaults on Karpenter provisioners for GPU fleets. For the hotfix, Marco/Samir can you propose a patched provisioner YAML?
Marco V: Draft snippet I plan to apply (will test in staging):
```
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-prod
spec:
  requirements:
    - key: "karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-family"
      operator: In
      values: ["p4","p3"]
  consolidation:
    enabled: true
  ttlSecondsUntilExpired: 600
  provider:
    capacityTypes: ["on-demand"]
```
Samir: Looks good. Suggest adding `limits: resources: cpu: "2000", memory: "1Ti"` to avoid runaway pods requesting absurd resource combos that force new launches.
Alex Chen: Thanks — please coordinate a short maintenance window to apply to prod and watch the first 2 hours. I'll mute alerts for that window to avoid noise.
Dina L: I'll add dashboards for ENI consumption and instance launch failure rate so we can quickly see if the change helps.
Priya Rao: Assigning action items: Marco + Samir = apply hotfix to prod (after staging test). Dina = dashboards. Alex = mute alerts + monitor cost. I'll file RFC.
Alex Chen: Thanks team. Let's discuss post-mitigation in tomorrow sync, bring data (node counts, ENI usage, invoices). :thumbsup:
